competitive_position.claim: MSG Entertainment operates a portfolio of iconic live entertainment venues in New York City and Chicago with seating capacities ranging from 2,800 to 21,000, owning Madison Square Garden, the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, and The Chicago Theatre while leasing Radio City Music Hall and the Beacon Theatre.

With seating capacities and configurations that range from 2,800 to 21,000, our diverse collection of venues enables us to showcase a multitude of acts and events that cover a wide spectrum of genres to diverse audiences.
The Company owns The Garden, the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, and The Chicago Theatre, and leases Radio City Music Hall and the Beacon Theatre.

competitive_position.claim: MSG Entertainment strengthens its commercial positioning through sponsorship sales representation agreements with MSG Sports, multi-year corporate suite and club licenses with annual escalators at The Garden, and a proprietary database of millions of customers.

competitive_position.claim: The Company faces intense competition across live entertainment venues and broader leisure options for discretionary spending and a limited pool of popular artists, requiring continuous technology investment and competitive pricing.
quotes: Our business competes, in certain respects and to varying degrees, with other leisure-time activities and entertainment options, such as television, radio, motion pictures, sporting events, music festivals and other live performances, restaurants and nightlife venues, the Internet, social media and social networking platforms, and online and mobile services, including sites for online content distribution, video on demand and other alternative sources of entertainment and information, in addition to competing for concerts, family shows, sporting events and other events with other event venues, for total entertainment dollars in our marketplace.

There may be a limited number of popular artists, groups or events that can attract audiences to our venues, and our business would suffer to the extent that we are unable to continue to attract such artists, groups and events to perform at our venues.
In order to maintain the competitive positions of The Garden and our other venues, we must invest on a continuous basis in state-of-the-art technology.
In addition, we must maintain a competitive pricing structure for events that may be held in our venues, many of which have alternative venue options available to them in New York and other cities.

competitive_position.claim: Revenue and profitability are concentrated in the Christmas Spectacular, whose 2025 production accounted for 18% of Fiscal Year 2026 revenues, and depend partly on the popularity and on-court or on-ice success of the Knicks and Rangers.

As a result of our commercial agreements with MSG Sports, the success of our business is also impacted in part by the popularity of MSG Sports’ Knicks and Rangers franchises with their fan bases and, in varying degrees, the teams achieving on-court and on-ice success, which can generate fan enthusiasm, resulting in additional suite, sponsorship, food and beverage and merchandise sales during the teams’ regular seasons.

competitive_position.claim: Because The Garden, the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, Radio City Music Hall, and the Beacon Theatre are all located in New York City, the Company faces greater exposure to local economic, regulatory, weather, and labor disruptions than more geographically diversified competitors.
quotes: The Company primarily operates in New York City and, as a result, is subject to greater degrees of risk than competitors with more operating properties or that operate in more markets.
The Garden, the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, Radio City Music Hall and the Beacon Theatre are all located in New York City.

competitive_position.claim: Proposed Penn Station redevelopment threatens operational disruption at The Garden and the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, and a non-binding memorandum of understanding announced in June 2026 contemplates transferring the Infosys Theater to the Master Developer.
quotes: On June 8, 2026, in connection with the proposed redevelopment of Penn Station, the Company announced it had entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Master Developer, which was previously selected by The National Railroad Passenger Corporation (“Amtrak”) to redevelop Penn Station, subject to the execution of various binding agreements (the “Developer Agreements”), contemplating the transfer of the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden to the Master Developer and acknowledging that The Garden must remain fully operational at all times as required by the Company, subject to further negotiation and execution of definitive documentation between the Company and the Master Developer and the execution of the Developer Agreements.

Regardless of the terms of the Developer Agreements and the completion of the redevelopment of Penn Station, that redevelopment may disrupt the operations of The Garden and the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden, which may adversely affect our business and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: The Garden's operations depend on renewing a zoning special permit originally granted in 1963 and most recently renewed in September 2023, which government officials and interest groups may use to press for Penn Station concessions or costly capital expenditures.
quotes: The Garden requires a zoning special permit, which was originally granted by the New York City Planning Commission in 1963 and most recently renewed in September 2023 for five years.

Certain government officials and special interest groups have in the past used, and may in the future use, the renewal process for the zoning special permit to pressure us to make concessions such as financial contributions to the redevelopment of Penn Station or relocating or transferring all or portions of the Madison Square Garden Complex.

There can be no assurance regarding the future renewal of the special permit or the terms thereof (including requirements for us to make significant capital expenditures as a condition to renewal of the permit), and the failure to obtain such renewal or to do so on favorable terms would have a material negative effect on our business.

competitive_position.claim: Calls and legislation introduced by New York state senators in January 2025 to repeal The Garden's property tax exemption threaten the Company's economics because, while the Knicks and Rangers cover 100% of property taxes, a repeal would trigger a percentage reduction in their annual license fees.
quotes: Further, in January 2025, four New York state senators introduced legislation to discontinue the real property tax exemption for The Garden.

Under the Arena License Agreements, the teams are responsible for 100% of any real property or similar taxes applicable to The Garden, however, if the tax exemption is repealed or the teams are otherwise subject to the property tax due to no fault of the teams, the annual license fee payable by the teams in connection with their respective use of The Garden will be reduced on a percentage basis as set forth in the Arena License Agreements.

competitive_position.claim: The Company's long-term leases for the Beacon Theatre and Radio City Music Hall expire in 2036 and 2038, respectively, exposing operations to renewal and landlord-dispute risks as well as a net-worth maintenance requirement on the Radio City Music Hall lease guarantor.
quotes: We lease the Beacon Theatre and Radio City Music Hall under long-term leases that expire in 2036 and 2038, respectively.

If we are unable to renew our lease agreements on economically attractive terms, if we, our affiliates or our landlords breach certain of the terms of these agreements, or if disputes otherwise arise with our landlords, our operations could be disrupted, we could be liable for monetary damages and our business could be materially negatively affected.

MSG Entertainment Holdings, the entity that guarantees the lease for Radio City Music Hall, is also required to maintain a certain net worth that, if not maintained, would require the entity to post a letter of credit or provide cash collateral.

competitive_position.claim: Ticket, suite, concession, merchandise, and sponsorship demand is sensitive to recessions, tariffs, and consumer spending pullbacks, while inflation increases labor and operating costs that the Company may not be able to offset with higher pricing.
quotes: Our business depends upon the ability and willingness of consumers and businesses to purchase tickets at our venues, license suites and club memberships at The Garden, spend on food and beverages and merchandise, and drive continued sponsorship and signage revenues, and these revenues are sensitive to general economic conditions, recession, fears of recession and consumer behavior, including due to the impacts of tariffs.
In addition, inflation, which has risen significantly in recent years, has resulted in and may continue to result in increased operational costs, including labor costs.

competitive_position.claim: Concerts and live events at the Company's venues require public performance licenses from music performing rights organizations, and an inability to renew them on historical terms or pass higher royalties to promoters could harm operating results.
quotes: We are required to obtain public performance licenses from music performing rights organizations, commonly known as “PROs,” in connection with the performance of musical works at concerts and certain other live events held at our venues.
If we are unable to obtain these licenses, or are unable to obtain them on terms consistent with past practice, it may have a negative effect on our business and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Shared officers and directors—including Executive Chairman and CEO James L. Dolan—across Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers, MSG Rangers, and AMC Global Media, together with corporate-opportunity waiver provisions in the charter, create potential conflicts over acquisitions, opportunities, and commercial disputes.
quotes: The Company’s Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, James L. Dolan, also serves as the Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers and MSG Rangers and as Non-Executive Chairman of AMC Global Media.

For example, there will be the potential for a conflict of interest when the Company or Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers, MSG Rangers or AMC Global Media look at certain acquisitions and other corporate opportunities that may be suitable for more than one of the companies.

Also, conflicts may arise if there are issues or disputes under the commercial arrangements that will exist between Sphere Entertainment, MSG Knickerbockers, MSG Rangers or AMC Global Media, on the one hand, and the Company, on the other hand.

As a result of our commercial agreements with MSG Sports, the success of our business is also impacted in part by the popularity of MSG Sports’ Knicks and Rangers franchises with their fan bases and, in varying degrees, the teams achieving on-court and on-ice success, which can generate fan enthusiasm, resulting in additional suite, sponsorship, food and beverage and merchandise sales during the teams’ regular seasons.
And later today, the Christmas Spectacular production begins its 2026 holiday season at Radio City Music Hall with 231 planned performances as compared to 215 in fiscal 2026.

risks.basis: stated in P2, with counter-evidence stated in F2, P1, P3, P4, and P5
risks.claim: Heavy geographic concentration in New York City leaves the company vulnerable to local disruptions, macroeconomic downturns, cost inflation, tariffs, and intense competition for audiences and artists.
quotes: The Company primarily operates in New York City and, as a result, is subject to greater degrees of risk than competitors with more operating properties or that operate in more markets.
In addition, inflation, which has risen significantly in recent years, has resulted in and may continue to result in increased operational costs, including labor costs.

risks.claim: Venue operations depend on retaining liquor licenses and obtaining third-party music performing rights organization (PRO) licenses, and the New York State Liquor Authority has previously threatened license revocation.
quotes: Failure to receive or retain, or the suspension of, liquor licenses or permits could interrupt or terminate our ability to serve alcoholic beverages at the applicable venue and could have a material negative effect on our business and our results of operations.

For example, the New York State Liquor Authority has in the past threatened to revoke certain of the Company’s liquor licenses, alleging that the Company’s policy of temporarily excluding adverse attorneys from entering its venues during the course of ongoing litigation violates New York state beverage laws.

risks.claim: Developing or enhancing proprietary productions and acting as a show promoter or co-promoter exposes the company to unrecouped upfront investments and deferred cost write-offs, as seen in a past $75.4 million write-off.
quotes: For example, we wrote off approximately $75.4 million of deferred production costs across Fiscal Years 2016 and 2017 related to the New York Spectacular Starring the Radio City Rockettes.
If we serve as promoters or co-promoters of a show, we have economic risk relating to the event.
